## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: getting the license and probationary rules
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The skills exam lists separate score-reducing errors from automatic failures; the two lists are kept apart in C so a minor error is never taught as an automatic fail [A01].
The manual states two different phone rules: the probationary paragraph bars any telecommunications device use while driving except a 911 call [A04], while the public safety paragraph bans typing, sending or reading texts and email unless hands-free or voice-operated [A05]; both are reported as printed and the conflict is flagged (verify IN-LICENSE-D-PHONE).
The licensed instructor exception to the passenger rule names an instructor license holder without saying the instructor must be on duty; no extra condition is added [A04].
Form numbers, mail delivery times and update channels are service details that can change and are isolated as dynamic [A05].

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 15 says Indiana law bars all drivers, probationary holders included, from driving while using any telecommunications device except for a 911 call, while physical page 16 bans only typing, sending or reading texts or email unless hands-free or voice-operated; confirm the current statute wording with an official Indiana source before teaching a single rule.
